newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Nine Indonesian leftists jailed for subversion.
newsitem.headline: Nine Indonesian leftists jailed for subversion.

text.p: Nine Indonesian leftists convicted on subversion charges were jailed for up to 13 years on Monday for membership in the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD).
The PRD members arrested in the wake of riots in Jakarta in July last year had faced possible death sentences under Indonesia's controversial subversion law.

Only three political parties currently campaigning for May 29 general elections are legally recognised in Indonesia. The PRD, whose members went underground after the arrest of their leaders, never received legal recognition.

Central Jakarta State Court judges, in announcing their verdict on PRD chairman Budiman Sudjatmiko, 26, said that while he had committed a serious crime which deserved heavy punishment, they did not agree with the prosecutors' demand for 15 years imprisonment.

"It is already proved that Budiman Sudjatmiko committed a criminal action under the main charge of subversion. As a result we sentence him to 13 years jail, less the time spent in custody," judge Syoffian Sumantri said at the end of the 3-1/2-hour judgement.
"We reject the verdicts as the court does not have the legitimacy to sentence us," Sudjatmiko told reporters from his holding room after his sentencing.

The other eight defendants received sentences ranging from 12 years to 18 months in prison. Last week, three PRD activists in Indonesia's second city of Surabaya received between six and four years on the same charges.
Two other defendants are still on trial.

"The message to the community is clear. Whoever has a different opinion from the government and who is thought to be behind events will be heavily punished," a lawyer with the non-governmental Legal Aid Institute (LBH), Bambang Widjojanto, told reporters outside the court.

As the sentences were being read more than 100 PRD sympathisers scuffled with police outside the Central Jakarta State Court but later dispersed. Witnesses said police beat and detained three PRD supporters.
The prosecution's case rested on PRD documents as well as its activities in organising strikes and public speeches.
The prosecutors said that while the defendents had no direct connection with the Jakarta riots, they had defamed President Suharto and undermined government institutions.
